transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have two courtyard set options on the table for Soundstage 3 — a masonry build or a modular painted-timber approach. Before I make a final decision on the construction plan, I want to hear from each of our representatives. Structural, permits, stunt coordination, and insurance — please give me your reports so we can move forward. Our approved budget is $180,000, and fabrication needs to begin after this review.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share my structural findings from yesterday's load test. The masonry courtyard option would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit, so that design is not viable as-is. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still working through the engineering queue, so I wanted to make sure this information is on the table now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share what I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning. The approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. The permit clerk's email hasn't been added to the production file yet, but these are hard constraints we need to factor into the decision.
